thread:
customer_john: Hey team — our checkout is failing starting ~2024-11-14T10:12:00 PDT. Getting 500s with 'tool-args-invalid' when invoking the payment tool, and we noticed duplicate charges (multiple charges for same order). Can someone look?

support-sophie: Sorry about that — can you paste a sample request body and any client SDK version? Also request_id if you have it.

customer_john: Using sdk-js v1.2.0. Sample request (redacted token):
```json
POST /v1/run
Authorization: Bearer REDACTED
{
  "model": "redwood/gpt-pay-1",
  "input": "charge",
  "tool": "charge-card",
  "args": "{\"orderId\":\"ORD-1234\",\"amount\":499}"
}
```
Note: our code expects args to be object but SDK seemed to stringify earlier. Request id: rq_20241114_abc123. Also saw intermittent 429s from auth service around same time.

support-sophie: Hmm that `args` is stringified and I don't see a `user_id` field — the tool schema requires `user_id` (string) and `orderId` (string). Can you share server-side error log for rq_20241114_abc123?

customer_john: Server log for rq_20241114_abc123: `ERROR runtime: tool invocation failed: invalid args shape: missing required key user_id; received type string for args`
Also our client retried on 500s (backoff 500ms -> 2s) and we see 3 charges for the single order.

deploy-bot: Deploy notice: strict-arg-validation flag toggled ON in production on 2024-11-14T02:00 by rollout/strict-args (release 2024.11.14-argfix).

maya: That deploy likely hardened parsing — previously the runtime silently accepted stringified JSON for args. Now strict validation rejects it, which explains the 500s. The missing `user_id` explains the schema error. The auth 429s may have triggered the client to retry earlier and then hit the strict validation.

eng-runtime-lead: Confirming — we enabled strict arg validation to prevent malformed tool payloads. We returned a 500 with message `tool-args-invalid` when `args` is not an object or required fields absent. Previously we coerced strings into JSON, which masked client issues. We will roll a short-term compatibility flag to loosen validation for the affected tool.

sre_tom: Observed traffic: p95 for /v1/run increased from ~1.2s to ~14s at spike time, and retry rates (5xx-triggered retries) jumped x6. Billing telemetry shows ~2.8x normal token usage for the customer between 10:10-10:20 — estimated extra $3.7k. Recommend: 1) enable lenient parser for `charge-card` for 1h 2) advise customer to add idempotency-key header and 3) investigate auth service 429s.

support-sophie: Repro steps we can share with eng and the customer (minimal):
```bash
# bad (stringified args) -> triggers 500
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/run \n -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \n -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n -d '{"model":"redwood/gpt-pay-1","tool":"charge-card","args":"{\"orderId\":\"ORD-1234\",\"amount\":499}'}'

# good (object args) -> should succeed
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/run \n -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \n -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n -d '{"model":"redwood/gpt-pay-1","tool":"charge-card","args":{"orderId":"ORD-1234","amount":499,"user_id":"user-998"}}'
```

customer_john: Thanks — we'll patch SDK usage asap. ETA for the lenient toggle? We need to stop the billing bleed now.

eng-runtime-lead: I can flip the compatibility flag for `charge-card` in 30m (manual toggle via internal console). That will accept stringified args and attempt to parse; it will still validate presence of `user_id` after parsing. We'll also add a quick telemetry hook to emit a metric when stringified args are parsed so we can monitor clients that need fixes. Permanent fix rolling in next deploy window (48h).

sre_tom: I'll ring-fence the customer's traffic to avoid broad impact and add a temporary rate-limit for anonymous retries. Also adding a billing alert to refund obvious duplicate charges post-mortem.

support-sophie: Action items: 1) @eng-runtime-lead toggle lenient parser for `charge-card` (ETA 30m) 2) @customer_john add idempotency-key + send any duplicate charge tx ids to support for refund flow 3) @sre_tom investigate auth 429 root cause.

customer_john: Appreciate it — we'll send transaction ids in ~15m. :thumbsup:

maya: I'll follow up after the toggle and confirm we see reduced 5xxs for rq_20241114_*.

eng-runtime-lead: Toggle done (2024-11-14T10:40). Monitoring now.

customer_john: Confirmed — 5xxs stopped and no new duplicates since ~10:41. Thanks everyone.

support-sophie: Closing loop — we'll coordinate refunds and timeline for the permanent SDK guidance.
